children: A group of banks led by Morgan Stanley Private

received a $1.3B loan from private credit lenders to finance L Catterton's acquisition of Fullscript after the underwriters failed to find buyers in the leverage finance sector, according to a media report on Tuesday.
Morgan Stanley syndicated the debt to direct lenders, including Blue Owl Capital Inc.
, and Antares Capital, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The loan was agreed to at four percentage points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate and a discounted price of $0.96 on the dollar, the people told Bloomberg. The loan from private credit lenders replaces the debt commitments made by the Morgan Stanley
-led group, which would have had to fund the deal otherwise. The banks had committed to a maximum pricing level of four percentage points over the benchmark rate.
Bloomberg had previously reported that interest from leveraged loan investors was insufficient to finance the deal by that route. Additionally, Morgan Stanley
provided a $230M revolving credit facility, the people told the news outlet.

When underwriting debt commitments, banks then seek to sell that debt to the high-yield bond and leveraged loan markets before the acquisition closes, which generates fees for the underwriters. But if demand sours for such debt, the banks can end up funding the debt themselves, adding the burden to their balance sheets.
In September, Fullscript announced that L Catterton, in partnership with Atlas Partners, would purchase a majority stake in the company from HGGC and Snapdragon Capital Partners.

title: Morgan Stanley-led group gets $1.3B loan from private credit for Fullscript deal - report
